Cyber Law & Cyber Crimes Simplified | Practical Guide with AI-Enabled Cyber Crimes Coverage | 8th Edition 2026

Cyber Law & Cyber Crimes Simplified is a practical and easy-to-understand guide authored by one of India's most recognized cyber law experts. The book bridges the gap between legal theory and real-world cybercrime challenges by covering cyber offences, digital evidence, data privacy, online investigations, and emerging AI-enabled cyber crimes. It is particularly useful for advocates, law students, police officers, compliance professionals, corporate legal teams, cybersecurity practitioners, and anyone seeking a clear understanding of India's cyber law framework.

Business Champ | A Complete Roadmap to Transform Your Business

Business Champ is a practical business transformation guide written by Chartered Accountant, entrepreneur, and business mentor Malay Damania. Drawing from more than three decades of advising business owners, the book combines entrepreneurial mindset, leadership, team building, communication, financial discipline, and growth strategies into a structured roadmap. Unlike theoretical management books, it focuses on real-world challenges faced by MSMEs, startups, family businesses, and growing enterprises. An excellent resource for entrepreneurs seeking sustainable growth and better business decision-making.

The Bench, the Bar and the Bizarre

If you think the law is always solemn and predictable, this book politely disagrees—and then proves it with style. The Bench, the Bar and the Bizarre takes you into the lesser-seen corners of the legal world, where logic sometimes takes a coffee break and reality feels stranger than fiction.

Through a series of real-life courtroom episodes, Tushar Mehta presents a fascinating blend of wit, absurdity, and insight. From unconventional judicial behavior to cases that stretch imagination, the book captures the unpredictable human side of law.

The Lawful and the Awful
Law is often seen as stern, structured, and serious—but this book flips the courtroom script. The Lawful and the Awful is a refreshing dive into the quirky, human, and sometimes bizarre side of the legal world.

Drawing from real courtroom episodes across jurisdictions, Tushar Mehta blends wit, sarcasm, and sharp observation to narrate stories where law meets personality—and sometimes loses the plot. From eccentric judges to unexpected courtroom moments, this book captures the lighter yet thought-provoking side of justice.

Stamp Duty Ready Reckoner and Market Value of Properties in Mumbai 2026-27

When it comes to property transactions in Mumbai, guesswork is expensive. This Ready Reckoner is your official-style compass—clear, updated, and built for real-world execution.

Before independence was won on the streets, it was fought inside courtrooms. Freedom on Trial brings to life twelve landmark cases that shaped India’s struggle against colonial rule—where law became both a weapon and a battlefield.

Written with depth and narrative power, this book captures how trials of freedom fighters were not mere legal proceedings, but turning points in India’s constitutional and political journey.

With a foreword by Justice D.Y. Chandrachud and endorsements from leading legal minds, this is more than history—it is a reminder of how law can define the destiny of a nation.

For lawyers, it offers perspective. For readers, it offers pride.

About the Book:
Some books don’t just explain law—they shape how we think about justice itself. A Theory of Justice by John Rawls is one of the most influential works in political and legal philosophy, redefining concepts of fairness, equality, and rights.

Through ideas like the “veil of ignorance” and justice as fairness, Rawls builds a framework that continues to influence constitutional thought, public policy, and legal reasoning worldwide.

For lawyers and law students, this is not just philosophy—it is the foundation behind many principles that courts interpret and apply.

Multiple Choice Questions for Judicial Service Examination

Multiple Choice Questions for Judicial Service Examination by Rajan Gunjikar is a focused and exam-oriented compilation designed specifically for Judicial Service aspirants. Covering key Minor Acts frequently tested in Civil Judge (Junior Division), District Judge, and Family Court examinations, this book equips candidates with objective-type questions that sharpen precision, speed, and statutory clarity. Authored by a former District Judge, the book reflects practical judicial insight aligned with competitive examination patterns.
Multiple Choice Questions for Judicial Service Examination – Major Acts

How to Handle GST Appeals – Practical Guide with Real-Life Case Studies

How to Handle GST Appeals is a practical, litigation-focused guide designed for professionals dealing with appellate proceedings under GST law. Authored by Adv. Md Samar, this 2026 edition combines statutory framework with real-life case studies to provide step-by-step clarity on drafting appeals, preparing grounds, handling hearings, and managing procedural compliance. For tax practitioners, advocates, and consultants, this book bridges the gap between theory and courtroom strategy in GST disputes.

featured_reviews.name: Janice Rodrigues
featured_reviews.review_text:
Ordered two books from the Long Game series by Rachel Reid from Fictionary online store under their “UK procurement” listing for ₹1798 total, and unfortunately the experience was extremely disappointing.

The books arrived in a torn paper bag with no bubble wrap or protective packaging at all. The books themselves also felt very poor in quality for the price charged, the covers felt like stiff paper/card stock instead of a regular paperback finish, the edges looked unevenly cut, and there was visible text bleed-through from the other side of the pages.

When I raised these concerns on WhatsApp, I was told “that’s how they were printed” and was offered a return. I paid from my own pocket to courier the books back and immediately shared photos of the packed return parcel as proof of the condition in which I sent them.

However, after that, the original number I had been communicating with stopped responding, and communication shifted to another number, where I was suddenly told the books had been received “torn and damaged” and that a refund could not be issued.

After multiple follow-ups and several days of silence, they eventually agreed to process the refund, but it has now been over 2 months and I still have not received my money.

Very disappointed with both the product quality and the customer service experience. Buyers should be cautious, especially when purchasing imported/procured books.

I’ve previously visited their physical store and had a few good online order experiences as well, which is why this situation was especially disappointing. Unfortunately, this particular order and the handling of the refund process were very poorly managed.

featured_reviews.name: Rishi Goswami
featured_reviews.review_text:
Je vous présente: Le Bazar des Rêves Brisés.

We arrived, hoping for a sanctuary: a haven of pristine contemplation where one might sip an artisanal coffee in the esteemed, silent company of literary legends—of Ginsberg's, of Plath's, of Keats. The aspiration, stamped into the glossy lease of this mall locale, was clearly to be a temple to the printed word.

The immediate reality, however, was a profound and shattering dissonance. The ambiance they desired to project was intellectual refuge; the reality they achieved was that of a fish market near a crowded railway station during a particularly raucous local festival. The air hummed not with quiet discovery, but with the high, frantic anxiety of total disorganization.

This establishment suffers from a chronic and debilitating lack of internal coherence. There is no evidence of management or any guiding organization—only the haphazard stacking of commerce upon chaos. It becomes apparent that the staff are not curating an experience but merely enduring a shift, their movements suggesting a perpetual, bewildered search for something misplaced, perhaps their own dignity.

The inventory, that sacred heart of any bookstore, is where the illusion completely dissolves. One searches, with quiet despair, for anything beyond "The Usual Suspects"—those run-of-the-mill, safe editions destined only for airports and bedside tables. The rare, the classic, the demanding titles are conspicuously absent, rendering the store’s literary pretensions hollow. Furthermore, the casual confirmation received on the phone regarding the availability of specific, requested books proved to be a lie, told perhaps out of habit or sheer, indifferent fantasy.

But the moment of ultimate, symbolic betrayal arrived not with a book, but with a beverage. In the middle of this poorly managed chaos, I spotted a small, tantalizing stack of Coca-Cola cans. Upon asking for one, I was delivered the definitive, breathtaking punchline: “No, that is for the owner. You must go down to the mall food court and get your own.”

To keep a product on display while simultaneously reserving it for the owner, denying the patron even the simplest act of commerce, is not merely bad service—it is a philosophical statement. It is a brilliant, miniature demonstration of utter lack of respect for the customer, revealing the entire venture as a mere show, designed for self-gratification rather than public engagement.

Coupled with a singularly uninspired coffee, and the unavoidable, crushing anonymity of its big mall location, this bookstore fails on every conceptual level. Go only if you seek an overwhelming sense of disappointment and a potent reminder that the purest acts of literature should perhaps remain strictly transactional and conducted at a distance. Welcome to the chaos.

featured_reviews.name: A K
featured_reviews.review_text:
The White Crow Books and Coffee: A Haven for Mumbai's Book Lovers!

Greetings, fellow bookworms! It's my pleasure to share my experience at The White Crow Books and Coffee, located in Mumbai's bustling Jio World Drive, BKC.

It's incredible how cozy and welcoming a great bookstore can be from the moment you walk in. The laid-back setting was perfect for escaping the city and reading a good book.

The book collection was impressive, to say the least. The curation of titles was well thought out and covered a wide range of genres, from classics to bestsellers and everything in between. As I browsed through the shelves, I was struck by the variety of books on display - there was something for every kind of reader.

But that's not all - The White Crow Books and Coffee also serves up some excellent coffee that's perfect for sipping on while you lose yourself in your favourite book. The coffee was rich and full-bodied and paired perfectly with the warm and inviting atmosphere of the bookstore.

What really caught my attention, though, was the cool curation of artworks tucked into the shelves. It was a refreshing change from the usual bookstore decor, and it added a touch of sophistication to the overall ambience.

The White Crow Books and Coffee is a must-visit for any bookworm in Mumbai. You can escape the city chaos and get lost in a good book here thanks to the great books, great coffee, and an inviting atmosphere.
